title: Extremely Sparse-View Computed Tomography from 2D Projections via Pose-Aware Diffusion Priors
claim: Existing approaches fail under extreme sparsity, either from artifacts or from needing dense training data; ours uses a single view per sample and wins.
layout: Left schematic of 3 pipelines; right 4x3 image grid with zoom insets
description: The left half is a schematic comparing three approaches in separate rounded panels: a) optimization-based, b) learning-based, and c) ours. A split person icon marks training versus inference, and extreme sparse-view scanner icons feed colored arrows (red and blue) into each panel. Panel a) goes from projections through 3D modeling and optimization to a reconstruction. Panel b) shows dense scanning, many projections, and reconstruction into volumes used to train a network. Panel c) shows single scanning with scanner-pose cues, a trained diffusion prior, and a frozen Novel View Synthesis module that produces projections for reconstruction. The right half is a grid of CT slices with orange zoom insets. Its columns are Optimization-based, Learning-based, Ours, and Ground Truth. The optimization-based column is blurry and noisy, and the learning-based column shows streak artifacts. Ours looks close to ground truth. Peach and orange accents set off our method.
caption: Tomographic reconstruction results from extremely sparse views at 0◦, 45◦, 90◦, 135◦. Current methods cover complementary sides of the extremely sparse view reconstruction problem: a) optimization-based methods [8] directly reconstruct from input views but produces severe artifacts when pushed to extreme sparsity at inference. b) Learning-based methods benefit from data-driven priors, but typically require reconstructed datasets from dense scannings that are difficult to obtain for certain applications. c) To simultaneously respond to the sparsity limit constraining both the training and inference process, our method learns a pose-aware projection-domain diffusion prior from a single 2D projection per training sample, then uses physics-guided sampling to produce tomographically consistent novel projections for accurate reconstruction.
abstract: Extremely sparse-view computed tomography (xSV-CT) is critical when scanning time, motion, or radiation tolerance limits each scan to only a few projections. In many such scenarios, the same acquisition limits also constrain dataset construction, making pre-reconstructed 3D volumes from dense scans unavailable. This exposes a gap in current sparse-view approaches: Optimization-based methods, which use the sparse measurements directly but lack data-driven priors to suppress artifacts, and learning-based methods, which use strong priors but usually require densely scanned training volumes acquired outside the xSV-CT regime. We study this train-sparse / infer-sparse setting by learning a pose-aware diffusion prior from one 2D projection per training sample, then guiding diffusion sampling with measured-view fidelity, shared-volume reprojection, and projection-physics consistency for tomographic reconstruction. On two public CT datasets across 1-, 4-, and 8-view settings, the proposed method achieves the best novel-view synthesis scores and best or competitive reconstruction quality compared with baselines that use dense-volume supervision.
